title: Add latency-aware quality-weighting and CI SLO enforcer
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a latency-aware quality weighting algorithm and a CI enforcer that gates PRs when SLO-weighted quality falls below project thresholds. Includes docs, tests, and a dashboard query for telemetry.
description:
Motivation: our current eval CI treats model quality and latency as independent signals. In practice, increased tail latency (p95/p99) often correlates with degraded quality for production prompts, and teams have been forced to choose between passing quality gates at the cost of unacceptable latency or failing fast on latency regressions while ignoring subtle quality changes.

What this PR does: introduces a latency-aware quality-weighting mechanism and a CI SLO enforcer that folds latency penalties into the quality score used by CI gates. The evaluator computes per-prompt quality metrics (accuracy/f1/semantic-similarity) as before, then applies a latency penalty function across configured latency buckets to produce a single weighted_quality metric. The CI hook compares weighted_quality against a per-project threshold and an allowable latency SLO.

Key design points: 1) Latency penalty is configurable via an exponential decay: penalty = exp(alpha * (latency_ms - bucket_center)/bucket_center) clipped to [0,1]. 2) Buckets are derived from historical percentiles (p50,p95,p99) by default; teams can override buckets in eval_config.yaml. 3) Weighted quality preserves interpretability by reporting breakdowns: raw_quality, latency_penalty, weighted_quality. 4) CI enforcer supports soft-fail mode (annotate + do not block) and hard-fail mode. Soft-fail is default for new projects. 5) Provides a backfill tool to recompute historical weighted_quality for dashboards and alert thresholds.

Files changed: adds core scorer at eval_harness/metrics/latency_weighted.py, a CI hook at ci/hooks/latency_quality_gate.py, integration test harness and unit tests under tests/, a docs page describing config and SLO semantics at docs/ci/latency-quality-slo.md, a dashboard SQL snippet, the CI workflow to run the new gate, and a short changelog entry.

Testing and validation: unit tests cover penalty math, bucket derivation, and config overrides. Integration tests run a synthetic prompt set with injected latency distributions to validate gate behavior across soft/hard modes and different thresholds. Benchmarks show median extra runtime of ~3ms per eval run (mostly from percentile aggregation); we ship a caching layer for historical percentiles to mitigate CI cost.

Backward compatibility: defaults to soft-fail and no penalty if latency history is unavailable. No mandatory changes required for existing eval configs.

Follow-ups: 1) Add a UI control in the Console for toggling soft/hard mode and tuning alpha per project (ENG-1107). 2) Explore per-cohort alpha tuning in a later PR.

review_comments:
Anika Shah (reviewer): Questioned the default alpha value and asked for a short guideline on how teams should pick alpha; requested a small table in docs with example alphas for typical latency profiles.
Maya (author): Added a guideline section and example table in docs; default alpha set conservatively to 0.002 with note to tune per-cohort.

Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Noted concern about noisy latency percentiles in small test sets causing flakiness; suggested adding a minimum-sample check and a cached historical baseline.
Maya (author): Implemented a sample_size threshold and cache for historical percentiles; integration tests updated to simulate cache warm/cold paths.

Priya Nair (reviewer): Asked for clarity on how the gate interacts with existing regression locks and whether it will block release automation.
Maya (author): Documented interaction and set soft-fail default; hard-fail requires explicit opt-in via eval_config.yaml.

Anika Shah (reviewer): Ran the new CI workflow on a noisy internal prompt set and requested an opt-out flag per-prompt-cohort.
Maya (author): Added cohort-level opt-out in the config and corresponding tests.

merge_result: Merged by Maya Patel via squash on 2024-11-12. Squash commit message: add latency-aware quality weighting + CI enforcer. No manual conflicts.
notes_summary: Introduces a configurable latency penalty that is folded into quality scores for CI gating. Default is non-blocking (soft-fail). Adds tests, docs, caching and a dashboard query. Follow-ups include Console controls and per-cohort tuning.
